standard_prerequisites.name: Fiber sequence of a pointed map
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a pointed map f : X \to Y the fiber F \defeq \hfib f {y_0} sits in a fiber sequence in which the next maps are \proj1 and the loop of f.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the input of the theorem (source lines 1080-1081).

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of a sequence of pointed sets
standard_prerequisites.statement: A sequence of pointed sets is exact at the middle term when the image of one map is contained in the kernel of the next and conversely.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what the proof establishes for the 0-truncations (source lines 1102-1108).

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy groups as truncated loop spaces
standard_prerequisites.statement: \pi_k is the 0-truncation of the k-fold loop space, so it is a group for k \ge 1 and abelian for k \ge 2 by the Eckmann-Hilton argument.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the group structure asserted in the statement (source lines 1119-1120).

core_obligations: Show that the 0-truncation of a fiber sequence is exact, i.e. that im(\trunc0g) is contained in ker(\trunc0f) and conversely, for an adjacent pair of maps with g \defeq \proj1 (source lines 1101-1108).
Prove the first inclusion from functoriality of \trunc0 together with f \circ g = 0 (source line 1110).

Prove the second inclusion by assuming w' : \trunc0 W with \trunc0f(w') = \tproj0{z_0}, reducing first to w' = \tproj0 w because the goal is a mere proposition, then using thm:path-truncation to turn the projected equality into an element of \trunc{-1}{f(w)=z_0} and a further truncation induction to get p : f(w)=z_0, so that (w,p) maps to w' (source lines 1111-1115).

Assemble the long exact sequence from the exactness of the 0-truncations, record the group and abelian-group structure from Eckmann-Hilton, and identify the maps through thm:fiber-of-the-fiber (source lines 1117-1123).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the theorem to exactness of the 0-truncation of a fiber sequence.
First inclusion: the composite is zero by functoriality.
Second inclusion: truncation induction plus the path-truncation equivalence.
Build the long exact sequence, its group structure and the identification of its maps.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 1080-1093 (book Theorem 8.4.6): a pointed map f : X \to Y with fiber F gives a long exact sequence of homotopy groups, which are groups except in the last three terms and abelian except in the last six. The statement records only the sequence and the algebraic structure, while the proof (source lines 1100-1129) has to establish exactness at every term: it reduces the theorem to exactness of the 0-truncation of a fiber sequence, proves the inclusion im \subseteq ker from functoriality together with f \circ g = 0, and then has to show ker \subseteq im for an element given only as a truncated equality, which forces two successive truncation inductions: one to lift the element of the 0-truncation to an element w of W, and one that uses the path-truncation equivalence to turn \tproj0{f(w)} = \tproj0{z_0} into a genuine path p : f(w) = z_0, after which (w,p) is the required preimage. The identification of the later maps with the negative of the induced maps on homotopy groups, and the resulting group and abelian-group structure, are then read off with thm:fiber-of-the-fiber and the Eckmann-Hilton argument; nothing of this reduction is visible in the statement.
